Choice A is correct. It's given that the kinetic energy, in joules, of an object with mass $6$ kilograms traveling at a speed of $v$ meters per second is given by the function $E$, where $E(v) = 3v^{2}$. It follows that in the equation $E(15) = 675$, $15$ is the value of $v$, or the speed of the object in meters per second, and $675$ is the kinetic energy of the object, in joules, at that speed. Therefore, the best interpretation of $E(15) = 675$ in this context is the object traveling at $15$ meters per second has a kinetic energy of $675$ joules.
